questions.prompt: Which EEG frequency range defines theta activity?
questions.rationale: Theta activity is defined by a frequency range of 4-7 Hz.

questions.prompt: During N2 sleep, a K-complex is followed by a brief burst of EMG activity and a shift to faster EEG frequencies lasting 2 seconds. How should this be scored?
questions.rationale: A scored arousal requires an EEG frequency shift lasting at least 3 seconds, so a 2-second shift does not meet arousal criteria.

questions.prompt: A patient has an arousal immediately after a respiratory event and then a leg movement. Which event should usually be considered first in sequence interpretation?
options: Respiratory-related arousal with a subsequent movement
questions.answer: Respiratory-related arousal with a subsequent movement
questions.rationale: Respiratory events often trigger arousal and movement, so sequence matters.

questions.prompt: According to AASM scoring rules, a pediatric obstructive apnea is scored when the event lasts for at least:
questions.rationale: Pediatric obstructive apnea is scored using a duration of at least two missed breaths.

questions.prompt: In pediatric respiratory scoring, which concept differs importantly from adult scoring?
options: Events are breath-based and not always fixed to 10-second duration
REM is not scored in children
questions.answer: Events are breath-based and not always fixed to 10-second duration
questions.rationale: Pediatric respiratory scoring uses breath-based rules and differs from adult fixed-duration conventions.

questions.prompt: A pediatric event has absent airflow and absent effort, lasts less than 20 seconds, and is associated with arousal and desaturation. What is the best interpretation?
options: It may still meet pediatric central apnea criteria
It cannot be scored because it is under 20 seconds
questions.answer: It may still meet pediatric central apnea criteria
questions.rationale: Pediatric central-apnea scoring may allow shorter events when accompanied by associated consequences such as desaturation or arousal.

questions.prompt: A patient slept for 360 minutes and had a total of 120 respiratory events (apneas + hypopneas). What is their Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI)?
questions.rationale: AHI = 120 events / 6 hours of sleep = 20 events per hour.

questions.prompt: Which report value is most helpful for separating REM-predominant OSA from more uniform OSA across the night?
options: REM AHI compared with NREM AHI
questions.answer: REM AHI compared with NREM AHI
questions.rationale: Comparing REM and NREM event burden helps show whether obstruction is more prominent in REM sleep.

questions.prompt: A report shows mild overall AHI, but the study had almost no REM sleep and very little supine sleep. What is the best interpretation trap to avoid?
options: Assuming the study definitely overestimated severity
Assuming the study may have underestimated severity
Assuming REM never affects apnea severity
questions.answer: Assuming the study may have underestimated severity
questions.rationale: OSA can worsen in REM and supine sleep, so limited time in those conditions can make severity look lower than usual.
